what: Fox Corporation owns Fox News, the Fox broadcast network and 29 local TV stations, the Fox Sports networks including FS1, and the free streaming service Tubi. It was created in 2019 when the Murdoch family sold 21st Century Fox’s studios to Disney.
customers: Pay-TV and streaming distributors that pay fees to carry its channels, advertisers, and tens of millions of viewers of news, sports and free streaming.
money: Affiliate fees and advertising from Fox News, Fox Business and its cable sports channels.
Advertising and retransmission fees from the broadcast network and local stations, plus Tubi’s ad revenue.
moat: Fox News is the most-watched US cable news network by a wide margin, and Fox holds rights to the NFL, Major League Baseball and other live sports that still draw mass audiences. Live news and sports are the parts of TV least hurt by streaming.
risks: Cord-cutting keeps shrinking the number of pay-TV homes that pay for Fox News and FS1.
Sports rights costs keep rising; the NFL contract is the largest single cost.
Political advertising swings revenue: election years such as fiscal 2025 inflate profit.
Defamation and other legal risks around Fox News have cost hundreds of millions before.
opportunities: Free cash flow has averaged about $1.5–3B a year, and the share count fell from 570M in 2022 to 439M in 2026.
Tubi gives it a growing free streaming business without the costs of a subscription service.
Cash of $4.5B against $7.6B of debt is comfortable.
Twenty analysts average a target near $80, about 23% above the price.
watch: Fox News ratings and affiliate fee renewals, and Tubi’s path to profit.
view: Fox is the most disciplined of the old TV companies: it sold its studios at the top, kept the parts of television that still work, news and live sports, and has used the cash to buy back almost a quarter of its shares since 2022. Free cash flow of $2.2 billion over the last twelve months against a $37 billion market value is about 6%.

The market prices it at about 14–15 times earnings, which reflects the long decline of cable TV. That decline is real, but Fox News loses viewers more slowly than general entertainment channels, and live sports keep advertisers paying. Fiscal 2025 profit was inflated by the US election, so the normal level is closer to fiscal 2026’s $1.7 billion.

This turns on how fast the cable bundle shrinks. Fox is not a growth stock, but it is a cash machine that keeps reducing its share count. I think it is fairly priced to slightly cheap, and a sensible holding for investors who want cash returns rather than growth.
bull: News and sports stay resilient, Tubi grows into a profit engine and buybacks keep shrinking the share count.
bear: Cord-cutting accelerates and rising sports rights costs squeeze profits.
